texts.preamble: Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 In The Court Of District Judge (Commercial Court)-01, Central, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi Presided By: Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal In The Matter Of: Cs (Comm) No. 2633-21 M/S Solar Sales (India) R/O. 44-B/Ua, Jawahar Nagar, Delhi-110 007 Also At: 902/290-291, Lane No. 4, Industrial Area, Shalimar Village, Delhi-110 088. ... Plaintiff Versus Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani Trading As M/S. Solar Gruh Udhyog, 188/3, G.I.D.C., Waghodiya-391760, Distt. Vadodara, Gujrat. ...Defendant Date of Institution : 02.08.2021 Date of reserving judgment : 31.08.2022 Date of Judgment : 10.10.2022 Suit For Permanent Injunction Restraining Infringement, Passing Of, Rendition Of Accounts Etc. Cs (Comm) No. 2633/21 Page No. 1/15 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. Vide this judgment, I have to decide the present suit for per- manent injunction restraining infringement of trademark, passing off, rendition of accounts etc. filed by the plaintiff against the defendant. Sh. Vineet Jain, is stated to be the duly authorized to sign and verify the pleadings and institute the instant suit on behalf of plaintiff com- pany. The plaintiff had gradually broadened the area of business with the advance of time and now it includes variety of goods namely Cocoa, Sugar, Spices Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53828396/ 1 and condiments, Ketchup, Yeast, Mustard, Sauces, Noodles, Treacle, Jaggery, Custard Powder, Corn Flour powder, mix masala, baking powder, vinegar included in Class-30, non-alcoholic drinks, syrups, juices, oil, other preparations for making beverages falling in Class- 32 and also other allied and cognate goods. 3. It has been stated that plaintiff adopted the trademark/ trade name SOLAR in the course of trade and business in the year 1984. The plaintiff has been engaged in the aforesaid trade and business under the trademark/ trade name/label SOLAR. The plaintiff in or- der to acquire the statutory rights filed several trademark applica- tions for the registration of the said trademark/label not only in class 30 but also in classes 29, 31, 32, 35, 42 & 43. The plaintiff the pro- prietor of the trademark/trade name/lable SOLAR in relation to aforesaid goods/services. The plaintiff has been using the trademark/ trade name/label SOLAR continuously since its adoption upto the present time. The artistic work, colour combination, placement of words, get up and make up of trademark/trade name / label are unique and the plaintiff is the owner and proprietor in the artistic fea- tures in the trademark/ trade name/label SOLAR and the plaintiff holds copyright therein. 4. It has been further stated that plaintiff has been honestly, bonafidely and in the course of trade using its said trademark/trade name/label as proprietor thereof continuously, commercially, openly, exclusively and to the exclusion of others in the course of trade with- out any interruption and interference from any corner whatsoever and has built up envious, enormous and valuable trade, goodwill and reputation in respect thereof. The detail of year-wise sale of the plaintiff is furnished herein below: DETAILS OF YEAR-WISE SALE OF THE PLAINTIFF Financial Year Sale Amount in Rupees. 2006-07 1,10,76,687/- 2007-08 1,33,01,562/- 2008-09 1,61,72,048/- 2009-10 1,72,19,435/- 2010-11 1,95,64,091/- 2011-12 2,02,96,706/- 2012-13 2,68,54,596/- 2013-14 3,15,13,500/- 2014-15 4,41,94,746/- 2015-16 6,02,96,059/- 2016-17 7,28,86,838/- 2017-18 8,67,10,258/- 2018-19 9,84,63,197/- 5. That the plaintiff is very imaginative and innovative in its services, presentation, aesthetics, dcor and presentation of its products. Hence, the plaintiff has prayed for a decree of permanent injunction, passing off, delivery up, rendition of accounts, damages etc. 12. Though the defendants entered appearance through their counsel on 01.02.2013 but remained unrepresented thereafter and failed to file a written statement as well. The defendants were thus directed to be proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 04.10.2013and the plaintiffs permitted to file affidavits by way of ex-parte evidence.
texts.arguments: 2. Briefly stated the case of plaintiff as stands emanated from the plaint are that plaintiff is an old established business concern and known countrywide as is engaged in the trade and business of pre- pared, processed and preserved food products. The ideas and innovations as well as quality of services and goods of the plaintiff are highly appreciated by the Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53828396/ 2 customers and are in great demand amongst the public who keep encouraging the plaintiff to continuously bring up new innovations in the manner of presentation of its goods and services. 6. That the plaintiff's said trademark/trade name/label SOLAR has already become distinctive, eye catching and associated with the plaintiff and plaintiff's products. The plaintiff's said goods and business thereunder are highly demanded in the markets and have acquired a vast reputation there under. The said trademark/trade name/label SOLAR has acquired secondary significance denoting the said goods and business of the plaintiff and is recognized with the plaintiff alone. The plaintiff has also spent considerable amount on the advertisement of its brand name. Another firm M/s. Puranchand & Sons, the sister concern of the plaintiff firm, is also engaged in the distribution of the said goods/services of the plaintiff under the said trademark/label/name. 8. It has been further stated that the plaintiff has been continuously promoting its sale of said goods and business under its said trademark/trade name/label through different media and modes. The plaintiff has also advertised its products through promotional measures. As such the plaintiff has already spent substantial amount of money on the publicity of the said trademark/trade name/label and in consequence thereof the said trademark/trade name/label enjoys indelible, envious, solid, enduring and first class reputation in the market. The plaintiff also carries on the trade and business through its exclusive websites namely www.solarsalesindia.com and also through third party ecommerce marketplace namely www.indiamart.com and the elk. 9. It has been further stated that the plaintiff maintains the highest standard of quality and sale of its goods and business and in furtherance has obtained all necessary governmental licenses including the food safety license, license under food products, factory licensing certificate as well as registration of firms alongwith state and central sales tax registration certificates. It has been stated that due to the defendant's impugned activities, the plaintiff is suffering tremendously in trade and business and also in terms of goodwill and reputation and the plaintiff's said proprietary rights are being violating . The innocent purchasers are being deceived and irreparable loss and serious mischief is being caused to the plaintiff and to the trade and consuming public. Ld. counsel for plaintiff submitted that despite service defendant has not filed written statement, therefore, his defence is not on record and hence, judgment may be passed u/o 8 rule 10 CPC. 16. Order 8 rule 10 CPC provides that "Where any party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 1 or Rule 9 fails to present the same within the time permitted or fixed by the court, as the case may be, the court shall pronounce judgment against him, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit, and on the pro- nouncement of such judgment, a decree shall be drawn up." Thus Order 8 Rule 10 contemplates two contingencies, namely (I) where a party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 1 fails to present the same within the time permitted by the Court; and (2) where a party from whom a written statement is required under Rule 9, CPC fails to present the same within the time fixed by the Court. In Disney Enterprises Inc. & Anr. v. Balraj Muttneja &Ors. [CS (OS) 3466/2012 decided on 20th February, 2014], Hon,ble High Court has held that this Court is of the opinion that no ex parte evidence would be required in this matter. 17. The same has been reiterated by the Court in S. Oliver Bernd Freier GMBH & CO. KG v. Jaikara Apparels and Ors. In the case of Microsoft Corpora- tion v. Rajendra Pawar & Anr. reported as 2008 (36) PTC 697 (Del.), considering the aspect of punitive damages, it was held as be- low:- "22. Perhaps it has now become a trend of sorts, especially in matters pertaining to passing off, for the defending party to evade Court proceedings in a systematic attempt to jettison the relief sought by the Plaintiff. Such flagrancy of the Defendant's conduct is strictly deprecatory, and those who recklessly indulge in such shenanigans must do so at their peril, for it is now an inherited wisdom that evasion of Court proceedings does not de facto tantamount to escape from liability. Judicial Process has its own way of bringing to task such erring parties whilst at the same time ensuring that the aggrieved party who has knocked the doors of the Court in anticipation of justice is afforded with adequate relief, both in law and in equity. It is here that the concept of awarding punitive damages comes into perspective. 23. Punitive damages are a manifestation of equitable relief granted to an aggrieved party, which, owing to its inability to prove actual damages, etc., could not be adequately compensated by the Court. Theoretically as well as practically, the practice of awarding of punitive damages may be rationalized as preventing under compensation of the aggrieved party, allowing redress for undetectable torts and taking some strain away from the criminal justice system. Where the conduct of the erring party is found to be egregiously invidious and calculated to mint profits for his own self, awarding punitive damages prevents Also At vs Shambhu Dhanjibhai Sedani on 10 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53828396/ 7 the erring party from taking advantage of its own wrong by escaping prosecution or detection."
